answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a cipher as the anchor of the cost.
